title: Why we grade every product A to D — and what it means for your wallet
author: ReCircle team
summary_html: Our four-tier grading system takes the guesswork out of buying second-hand. Here’s exactly what each letter means.
body_html:
Buying a refurbished product should feel just as safe as buying new — which is why every item we list carries a condition grade from A to D.

Grade A — like new

Indistinguishable from new on handling. Zero functional issues. If there are any cosmetic marks at all, they’re only visible under close inspection.

Grade B — excellent

Light signs of previous use: maybe a hairline scratch, a small scuff on a corner. Fully functional, often with original packaging.

Grade C — very good

Visible but minor cosmetic wear. Perfect for buyers who care about price and performance over pristine looks.

Grade D — good / project

Character pieces. May have notable cosmetic flaws. Ideal for buyers who plan to personalise or use hard.

All grades come with the same ReCircle warranty. We don’t sell anything that doesn’t work.

title: The EU Digital Product Passport, explained — what merchants need to know before 2027
author: ReCircle team
summary_html: By 2027 every product sold in the EU will need a Digital Product Passport. Here’s how ReCircle has it covered on day one.
body_html:
Under the EU’s Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation (ESPR), most non-food goods sold in the EU will need a Digital Product Passport (DPP) by the end of 2027. Phones and consumer electronics are among the first-wave categories.

What a DPP contains

  • Materials and origin
  • Repair and refurbishment history
  • Warranty and end-of-life routing
  • Unique ID accessible via QR code

Why refurbished merchants are affected sooner

The Right-to-Repair and Circular Economy packages already impose traceability requirements. Adding a DPP to your refurbished listings today is a one-off effort that future-proofs you against 2026 and 2027 deadlines.

How ReCircle handles it

Every product in ReCircle has a recircle.dpp_id and recircle.dpp_url metafield. The product page renders a compact DPP block linking to the public record. Merchants keep using whatever DPP registry they prefer — ReCircle just displays it.

title: We saved 482 tonnes of CO₂e in 2024 — here’s the maths
author: ReCircle team
summary_html: Transparent methodology: how we estimate CO₂ avoided per product, and why the numbers are conservative on purpose.
body_html:
Every product page carries a CO₂ savings figure. Here’s how we calculate it.

Method

We use lifecycle assessments (LCAs) published by manufacturers and independent bodies (ADEME, Ellen MacArthur Foundation, Nature studies). For each category we take the lower-bound published estimate of cradle-to-gate CO₂e for a new unit, then subtract the refurbishment footprint (energy, replacement parts, shipping).

2024 totals

  • Electronics: 287 tCO₂e saved
  • Fashion: 142 tCO₂e saved
  • Furniture & appliances: 53 tCO₂e saved
  • Total: 482 tCO₂e

Full methodology and source list: Sustainability report.
